history.summary: Shakti shrine where, per the legend in the 8th-century Kalika Purana, the head of Goddess Sati (Parvati) fell as Lord Vishnu's Sudarshan Chakra dismembered her body carried by Shiva. The temple stands about 12 km from Malinithan towards Along (Aalo) in West Siang district; a sacred kund lies 100 m below the temple down a spiral path, famed for a glittering object visible from afar that disappears on approach, and its pond water is believed to have medicinal value. One travel-heritage source claims a Pala-period foundation around 1350 CE with Nagara architecture, but no scholarly or ASI source corroborates this — treat as unverified. Coordinates are approximate (offset from Malinithan temple towards Along), not a precise POI match — verify.

name: Akashiganga Temple
town_description: Malinithan is a village in Lower Siang district on the Assam border, best known for the 10th-12th century Chutia-era Malinithan temple ruins dedicated to Goddess Durga, a major archaeological site of Arunachal Pradesh. Nearby Likabali is the local market town and road junction on the route towards Along (Aalo).

travel.airport: Lilabari Airport (North Lakhimpur, Assam) is the nearest; Dibrugarh Airport (Mohanbari) is also cited as nearest to Malinithan
travel.railway: Naharlagun (Itanagar) is the nearest railhead in the state; most visitors travel by road from Assam
travel.road: Bus and car from Guwahati and Itanagar to Malinithan; the temple is 12 km towards Along (Aalo). Thrice-weekly Pawan Hans helicopter service runs Guwahati-Itanagar; there is a helipad at Along, about 25 km from the temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to April; avoid the monsoon (June-September) when landslides disrupt hill roads
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours are typical for this hill shrine, but no published darshan timings were found — verify before visiting
